items.explanation: The person who gets something takes para: es para ti.
optionNotes: Por is for a cause or a route, not for the person who gets something.
A ti means “to you”, not “for you” here.
De ti would mean “of you” or “from you”.

items.explanation: Thanks always take por: gracias por la invitación.
optionNotes: English “for” is not para after gracias.

items.prompt: Ahorro dinero ___ comprar una bicicleta. (I'm saving money to buy a bike.)
items.explanation: Purpose (in order to) is para + infinitive.
optionNotes: Por + infinitive gives a cause, not a purpose.
De is not used for a purpose.
A is not used for a purpose after ahorrar.

items.explanation: The means of communication takes por: por teléfono.
optionNotes: Para is for a goal, not a means.
Spanish says por teléfono, not en teléfono.
Spanish says por teléfono, not con teléfono.
